annotations.title: Get the scenes of a video

description: [Free] Reads this account. Returns the scene-by-scene plan of a video: what each scene narrates, its on-screen caption, how long it holds, and whether it is real footage of the page or a motion graphic (and which motion).
name: get_storyboard

duration_source.description: Whether duration_seconds (per scene and in totals) was measured on the last render or is still the plan. "rendered" only when every timed scene was measured; a scene added since the render keeps the film at "planned" and says so itself.
"rendered": duration_seconds was measured on the last render. "planned": it is the requested hold, not yet filmed. null when there is no duration at all.

inset.description: The presenter: generate, character, model, corner, shape, size, mute, clip_url (null until rendered), clip_seconds.

narration_seconds.description: How long the WORDS take to say. A scene's on-screen length is its slice of one continuous voice track, so this is usually shorter than duration_seconds — the difference is the pause between two sentences, not silence to be trimmed.

narration_seconds_estimate.description: How long the words SHOULD take, from the word count and this language's rate. Always present, including before the first render — narration_seconds is a measurement and is null until the voice exists.

raw_frame_url.description: The generated picture with no film over it, for create_character. null when the visual was NOT generated (a page screenshot is no character reference), so a film with no AI scenes is null throughout. To show a person the scene, use thumbnail_url.

totals.description: Speech over picture for the whole film; before the first render it is estimated from the words (coverage_is_estimated). Below about 0.7 there is visible dead air, but read the per-scene figures first: a healthy film has about a second of gap per scene.

title: Get the scenes of a video
